title: A dietary switch promotes sensory neuron-dependent cancer-associated cachexia.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: No data files exist to open. I checked: Europe PMC record (isOpenAccess=N, inPMC=N, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, no text-mined accessions beyond an RRID); PubMed elink from PMID 42391376 to GEO/SRA/BioProject/BioSample (zero links); OpenAlex (oa_status 'closed', no repository full text); PMC search for 'adz4196' (0 hits); GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) searches for cachexia+Lkb1 (0), cachexia+nodose (0), Stk11+high-fat-diet (1 unrelated series), and the senior author's 65 GEO series (newest are aortic aneurysm, LIF/LKB1 myeloid niche, ageing metastasis, cysteine deficiency - none is this paper); SRA and BioSample searches (nothing matching); Zenodo DOI/title search (0 hits); Dryad search (0 hits); and a direct HEAD on the Science supplementary PDF, which returned HTTP 403.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the biology comes from the 150-word abstract alone: Lkb1 (liver kinase B1) loss promotes cachexia in mouse lung cancer models, a high-fat diet paradoxically worsens sickness behaviour, tumour-derived prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) acting locally rather than through the bloodstream drives it, and ablating lung sensory neurons prevents it. I could not read the methods, the data availability statement, figure source data, or any supplementary table.

a1_downloadable.note: No downloadable dataset found anywhere. The article is closed access (no PubMed Central copy, no Europe PMC full text), its supplementary materials sit behind a publisher block (HTTP 403), and no accession for it exists in GEO, SRA, BioProject, BioSample, Zenodo or Dryad as of today. There is nothing to download, not even behind an application.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessable - no files. From the abstract, the plausible outcomes (body weight loss, food intake, sickness-behaviour scores) would live in per-figure source data if the supplement were reachable.

a5_enough_rows.note: Not assessable, but the unit of analysis in this study is a mouse. Preclinical cachexia experiments of this kind run tens of animals per arm, which is one to two orders of magnitude below the ~1,500-row bar; no row count was verified.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Whatever exists would be small tables plus a handful of RNA-sequencing count matrices; size is not the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot compare: no download and no accessible methods section.

a8_label_provenance.note: Not assessable. Abstract implies directly measured phenotypes (weight, intake, sickness behaviour), which would be fine provenance, but nothing was verified.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: this paper's measurements are not publicly available in any form I could retrieve.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use tumour genotype, diet and tumour gene expression to predict how much weight and appetite a tumour-bearing mouse loses.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-mouse records of tumour genotype (with or without Lkb1, a tumour-suppressor gene), diet (normal chow versus high-fat), treatment (prostaglandin-blocking drug, sensory-nerve ablation) and, where available, tumour gene expression. Number of mice: unknown, and almost certainly in the tens.
plain_idea.predict: Severity of wasting - body weight change, daily food intake, and a sickness-behaviour score - all measured directly on the animals in the laboratory.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cachexia researchers and oncologists would like to know which tumours will trigger wasting and whether feeding patients more fat helps or harms; a model linking tumour features to wasting severity would direct which interventions to test next. In practice, nothing can be learned here because the measurements are not released.

ml_idea: Considered and abandoned: predict per-mouse cachexia severity (weight loss, food intake, sickness behaviour) from tumour genotype, diet arm and tumour transcriptome. Dies immediately on data availability, and would die again on sample size even if the figure source data appeared.

effort.compute_note: No estimates possible: no files were obtainable, so there is nothing to size.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Look for an accession from this paper in GEO/SRA and try the supplement - both come back empty (zero linked accessions, HTTP 403 on the supplement). That check took minutes and killed it.

verdict_reason: Part A1 fails outright: the paper is closed access with no PubMed Central copy, its supplement returns HTTP 403, and no accession for it exists in GEO, SRA, BioProject, BioSample, Zenodo or Dryad. There is literally no data file to open. Even if the figure source data later appeared, the unit of analysis is a single mouse in a preclinical experiment, so A5 (enough rows) would almost certainly fail too.
